newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, focus on spot month.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, focus on spot month.

text.p: COMEX copper ended weaker on profit-taking, news of a settlement at Poland's KGHM producer, and liquidation of the spot March contract which went off the board Wednesday.
The cash to three months backwardation on LME also weakend to slightly to $53/$58.

Traders said there was good support at 110.00 cents a pound in the May COMEX contract. Low inventories and uncertainty over some production facilities such as Kennecott in the U.S. would continue to underpin the market, they added.
May COMEX went out 2.25 cents firmer at 110.65 cents a pound, traded 112.50 to 109.80 cents.
Volume was estimated at 18,000 lots, with switches estimated at 2,580.

Some dealers said there was some concern about the yawning spread between spot March and LME cash. The spread had ballooned to about 9 cents with open interest in the New York spot month seen as being high in the run up to expiry Wednesday.
The huge premium attracted some 20,000 short tons of metal from LME warehouses to their COMEX counterparts.

"Probably more would have been delivered if people holding the warrants in Long Beach would have let go of the metal. Why did they not move it to COMEX when they could make four cents (per pound)?" a dealer said.
Some consumers, who price on the average of the spot month, will have been hit by prices inflated by the ballooning New York spot premium.
The dealer said a complaint was made to the CFTC asking why NYMEX's COMEX division did not impose an extra margin on the March month to dampen the price surge in recent days.
A CFTC spokesman could not comment on the issue. NYMEX officials were not immediately available.
The surging spot month also had some impact on the scrap copper market.
"If you are selling copper scrap basis New York price to Japan, the arbitrage is making it extremely difficult because New York prices are way over London prices," an East Coast scrap merchant said.
With New York's eight-to-nine cent spot premium over LME cash, it almost made sense to buy the scrap in Europe for shipment to U.S. customers, the merchant added.
But relief is in sight for some - April, which becomes the spot month from Thursday, settled at 111.65 cents, just a cent above most-active May.
Meanwhile the board and trade unions at KGHM copper company agreed on a 17 percent wage hike. The unions will meet Thursday to decide whether a strike alert will now be dropped.
